title: Unbounded quasi-coherent descent on the face total site
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme and $Z$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-pc-scheme], [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Let $u:U_\bullet\to Z$ be an augmented simplicial algebraic space for which $U_0\to Z$ and all higher matching maps are flat, locally finitely presented and surjective; the matching object is the finite limit of proper faces and its first term is $U_0\times_ZU_0$. Discard the degeneracies and form the ringed total category $\mathscr M$ of [lem-sfb-semisimplicial-ringed-total-category] using for each $U_n$ the enlarged etale site $\mathcal C_{U_n}$ of algebraic spaces etale over $U_n$, with its extended structure sheaf, whose topos and module category are those of the small etale site $(U_{n,\mathrm{et}},\mathcal O_{U_n})$ [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model], and for an injective order map with structure morphism $h:U_n\to U_m$ the fibre-product functor $V\mapsto U_n\times_{U_m}V$ with its ring map; these give the canonical ringed morphisms of the small etale topoi, with coherent identity and composition comparisons [lem-trf-space-enlarged-ringed-composition-localization]. The augmentation is formed in the same way from $u_n:U_n\to Z$. Let $u$ also denote the induced ringed total augmentation. A total module is called quasi-coherent when its components are quasi-coherent [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module] and its transitions are isomorphisms. These modules form a weak Serre subcategory (closed under kernels, cokernels and extensions). A derived total object lies in $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathscr M)$, the full subcategory having quasi-coherent cohomology systems, if and only if it is cartesian and each $e_nB$ has quasi-coherent cohomology. The functors
$$Lu^*:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Z)\longrightarrow D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathscr M),\qquad Ru_*:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathscr M)\longrightarrow D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Z)$$
are mutually quasi-inverse triangulated equivalences, with their adjunction unit and counit isomorphisms. Derived direct image is computed by K-injective resolutions and pullback by K-flat resolutions. This holds for unbounded complexes, without quasi-compactness or separatedness assumptions on $Z$ or the $U_n$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-hypercover-augmentation-face-property] to the class of flat locally finitely presented surjections. Every face and augmentation component is flat, and every injective-order transition is a composite of faces, so all their module pullbacks are exact. By [lem-sfb-semisimplicial-ringed-total-category], $e_nu^*=u_n^*$ and evaluation is exact and jointly conservative. Consequently $u^*$ is exact: evaluate the image of a short exact sequence and use exactness of every $u_n^*$. The same total-category statement now says that cartesianness of a derived object is equivalent to invertibility of the transitions on each cohomology system. Since $e_nH^q(B)=H^q(e_nB)$, adding component quasi-coherence gives exactly the claimed characterization of $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathscr M)$.

source.place: 0DHF proof, first paragraph and Ad (1); use only faces, as supplied by the two cited nodes

proof.text: Write $\mathcal A$ for the cartesian componentwise quasi-coherent modules. Kernels and cokernels of maps in $\mathcal A$ are componentwise quasi-coherent by [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-kernels-colimits]; their transitions are isomorphisms because each face pullback is exact and thus carries the kernel and cokernel diagrams to the corresponding diagrams. For an extension of two such systems, [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-extension-closed] makes each middle component quasi-coherent. In the diagram of two short exact component sequences obtained along a face, the endpoint transitions are isomorphisms, so the middle transition is also: its kernel maps to zero in the quotient and then vanishes in the left term; a section of the target middle term lifts locally in the quotient and its remaining difference lifts in the left term. Thus $\mathcal A$ is closed under extensions. The same two quasi-coherence statements give these closures downstairs on $Z$. These are precisely the weak Serre conditions.

source.place: 0DHF proof, weak Serre paragraph; spaces-properties.tex 03M1, lemma-properties-quasi-coherent

proof.text: For the augmentation $u$, [lem-sfb-fppf-face-heart-descent] gives the equivalence $u^*:\operatorname{QCoh}(Z)\simeq\mathcal A$ with inverse $u_*$. For each $G\in\operatorname{QCoh}(Z)$, [lem-sfb-fppf-face-heart-derived-unit] gives the actual adjunction unit $G\xrightarrow{\sim}Ru_*u^*G$. These are the heart and degree-zero acyclicity hypotheses of the unbounded criterion, for the face total augmentation itself. Both cited statements use exactly the matching-map hypotheses in force here, and neither asks for flat degeneracies.

source.place: 0DHF proof, Ad (2)–(3); face adaptations of 0DHD and 0DHE

proof.text: Use the affine scheme objects $V\to U_n$ as a basis of each enlarged etale site, and hence of the total site; scheme charts and then affine open covers give these coverings by [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model]. Every covering of such a $V$ refines to a family with affine scheme domains by the same construction. The total and component module categories are Grothendieck by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck] and so have enough injectives by [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives]. By [lem-sfb-semisimplicial-evaluation-free-adjoint], evaluation $e_n$ has an exact left adjoint $\ell_n$. It therefore preserves injectives: extending a map into $e_nI$ across a monomorphism is adjoint to extending into $I$ across its monomorphic $\ell_n$ image. For $F\in\mathcal A$ apply $e_n$ to an injective resolution of $F$ in $\mathscr M$. It is an injective resolution of $F_n$ in the module sheaves on $\mathcal C_{U_n}$, and in each degree sections at the total-site object $V$ are literally the sections of that evaluated module at $V$. Taking cohomology identifies $H^p_{\mathrm{tot}}(V,F)$ with the derived module evaluation $H^p_{\mathcal C_{U_n}}(V,F_n)$.

source.place: 0DHF proof, Ad (4), affine-object basis and the comparison of total and component cohomology (lemma-sanity-check-modules), done here with the exact left adjoint of evaluation

proof.text: Let $W$ be $U_n$ or $Z$, let $F'$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_W$-module, transported to $\mathcal C_W$ by [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model], and let $v:V\to W$ be an affine scheme object. By [lem-pe-ringed-site-derived-evaluation-slice], applicable by the enough injectives of step 4, the derived module evaluation $H^p_{\mathcal C_W}(V,F')$ is the abelian cohomology of $F'|_V$ at the final object of the slice $\mathcal C_W/V$. By [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model], postcomposition identifies $\mathcal C_V$ with $\mathcal C_W/V$ with the same coverings, and restriction to the slice with module pullback along the localization morphism of $v$; [lem-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology-invariance-under-site-equivalence] transports the cohomology to $H^p_{\mathcal C_V}(V,\widetilde{v^*F'})$. The same model says that restriction to the scheme objects $V_{\mathrm{et}}\subset\mathcal C_V$ is an equivalence of sheaf categories leaving sections at scheme objects unchanged. An equivalence preserves injectives, so this group is $H^p(V_{\mathrm{et}},v^*F')$. The module $v^*F'$ is quasi-coherent by [lem-sfb-space-module-pullback-quasicoherent], hence $v^*F'\simeq G_{\mathrm{et}}$ for a Zariski quasi-coherent $G$ on $V$ by [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence]. Now [lem-sc-etale-affine-qcoherent] gives $H^p(V_{\mathrm{et}},G_{\mathrm{et}})=0$ for $p>0$. With step 4 ($W=U_n$, $F'=F_n$) this holds on the total site, and with $W=Z$ for every $F'\in\operatorname{QCoh}(Z)$ on $\mathcal C_Z$, for every affine domain of every refined covering, with the common bound $d_V=0$. Thus both local bound hypotheses hold; no finite cover or global cohomological bound is needed.

source.place: 0DHF proof, Ad (4)–(5), affine-object basis and bound zero; cohomology over an object as cohomology of the localized site (sites-cohomology.tex 03F3)

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-ringed-unbounded-descent-criterion] with source the face total ringed topos, target the enlarged etale ringed topos of $Z$, and weak Serre categories $\mathcal A$ and $\operatorname{QCoh}(Z)$. Steps 1–2 supply flatness and the weak Serre hypotheses, step 3 supplies its heart equivalence and derived unit on modules, and steps 4–5 supply its two local bound hypotheses. It follows that $Lu^*=u^*$ and $Ru_*$ are inverse triangulated equivalences on the full unbounded subcategories defined by these cohomology conditions, with the canonical unit and counit isomorphisms. The enlarged-site equivalences identify these with precisely the small-etale categories in the statement. In particular the result applies without boundedness, quasi-compactness or separatedness assumptions.

The total site and all component sites are small relative to the module universe. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck] makes their module categories Grothendieck, and [lem-sfb-grothendieck-k-injective] supplies K-injective resolutions. The definition [def-sfb-right-derived-functor] computes $Ru_*$ by applying $u_*$ to these resolutions. On the pullback side [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] gives unbounded K-flat resolutions with flat terms, and [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback] computes $Lu^*$ by termwise tensor pullback of them. Since $u^*$ is exact by step 1, these compute the already identified termwise functor. These statements apply to arbitrary complexes and require no extra geometric hypothesis.
